decisions.justification: Question 1 asked whether conflicts should reject the entire plan, skip steps, or advance numbering; the user selected whole-plan rejection with every conflict reported.
Question 4 asked how broadly no-partial-changes should apply, and the later transaction-model question led the user to choose an unchanged input plus atomic sibling-output publication.
Question 7 explicitly asked how exact self-mappings should behave, and the user chose successful no-ops that are not listed as changes.
Questions 3 and 9 asked whether a target occupied by another source scheduled to move should remain a conflict; the user chose rejection.
Questions 7 and architectural question 8 asked what repeated/self-only runs do; the user chose no publication and a `nothing changed` message.
The agent never asked whether case-only names clash or are no-ops, despite silently implementing Windows-specific case folding in `key()`.
Questions 2 and 9 asked about stdout, stderr, exit status, and diagnostic format; the user chose empty stdout on rejection, stable stderr lines, a summary, and nonzero exit.
Question 2 explicitly offered retaining the proposed plan on failed-run stdout versus printing nothing, and the user chose no preview output on rejection.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: a run that cannot complete leaves every file unchanged
no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session was unusually thorough and visibly implemented nearly every settled behavior, including atomic publication, collision rejection, no-op reruns, and the stream contract. It over-interrogated the user and delayed the whole-approach choice until after many detail questions; it also never surfaced the case-insensitive-filesystem decision, instead encoding an assumption in the implementation.
